findings.claim: ans: "Protected terms (Château, Clos, Cru, Vintage/Port, Classic…)"; exp: "Why an Aussie 'Port' became Tawny and 'Sherry' became Apera at home too."
findings.finalFix: ans: "Protected traditional terms (Château, Clos, Cru, Classic…) in the EU market without qualifying (meeting the EU conditions or a bilateral agreement)"; accept: ["chateau clos cru reserve in eu market", "protected terms like clos or cru"]; exp: "Not the same as GI protection: Port and Sherry are protected geographical indications, which is why Australian 'Port' became Tawny and 'Sherry' became Apera under the 2008 EU–Australia wine agreement (in force 1 September 2010), which also lets Australia keep tawny, ruby, cream and vintage."

findings.claim: Metallic clash risk comes from tannin and oak, not white wine per se.
findings.finalFix: High acid and a saline, mineral echo match the oyster's brine, and no oak with modest alcohol keeps the wine from swamping its delicacy. The fishy-metallic clash tracks the wine's iron (Tamura 2009), not tannin, oak or colour as such.

findings.claim: A quiet revolution: flor wine without the spirit returns to legality.
findings.finalFix:
ans: "Expanded the ageing zone to the whole production zone, readmitted six traditional grapes, and formalized categories (pagos, Fino Viejo, en rama); optional fortification was proposed then but only approved by the EU in 2025"
accept: ["ageing zone expanded grapes added", "ageing zone expanded to whole production zone", "expanded ageing zone new grapes en rama definition", "six old grape varieties readmitted ageing zone expanded", "pagos fino viejo en rama defined"]
exp: "The 2022 pliego (BOJA, October 2022) expanded the ageing zone to the whole production zone, readmitted six pre-phylloxera grapes, and defined pagos, Fino Viejo and en rama. Optional fortification for wines reaching 15% naturally (17% for Oloroso) was a major amendment in the same package. The EU approved it on 29 July 2025 and it came into force on 25 August 2025."
